name: Niagara Falls
hook: Honeymoons, barrels and hydropower: the border cataract with more stories than water.

facts.label: Horseshoe Falls
facts.statement: The falls are two cataracts: Horseshoe Falls on the Canadian side, named for its curved crest, and the straight American Falls.

facts.label: New York and Ontario
facts.statement: The falls sit on the U.S.–Canada border, between New York State and the Canadian province of Ontario.

facts.label: Annie Taylor
facts.statement: In 1901 schoolteacher Annie Taylor became the first person to go over the falls in a barrel — and survived.

facts.label: the honeymoon capital
facts.statement: Niagara was the original American honeymoon destination: Theodosia Burr honeymooned here in 1801 and started the tradition.

facts.label: Love Canal
facts.statement: The Love Canal neighborhood in Niagara Falls, New York, became the symbol of toxic-waste disaster after chemicals leaked there.

facts.label: hydropower
facts.statement: The falls have generated electricity since the 1890s; by 1896 Niagara power reached Buffalo, about 20 miles away.

facts.label: seven miles of erosion
facts.statement: Since forming about 10,000 years ago, the falls have eaten back some seven miles of cliff.
